title: System Protocol 2: Comparison Operators
lessonSummary: You now master all six comparison operators – and you know that = assigns and == compares.

tasks.instruction: Run this example. It shows all comparisons and prints True or False for each.
tasks.codeTemplate:
value = 42
print(f"Value: {value}")
print(f"{value} < 50: {value < 50}")
print(f"{value} <= 42: {value <= 42}")
print(f"{value} > 30: {value > 30}")
print(f"{value} >= 42: {value >= 42}")
print(f"{value} != 42: {value != 42}")

rank = 15
if rank == 15:
    print("Correct: Rank 15 reached")

tasks.instruction: The variable speed is already created. Use a comparison to check whether it is greater than 1000, and then print: Faster than light!
tasks.codeTemplate:

# 🎯 Your solution here:

title: System Protocol 5: and, or, not
lessonSummary: Combined conditions: and demands everything, or needs just one, and not flips the result.

tasks.instruction: Run this example. It shows and, or and not.
tasks.codeTemplate:
has_access_code = True
has_fingerprint = True
if has_access_code and has_fingerprint:
    print("Access to the command deck granted!")

has_emergency_key = False
has_override_code = True
if has_emergency_key or has_override_code:
    print("You can open the door manually!")

alarm_active = False
if not alarm_active:
    print("No danger – all systems secure!")
